newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds finished active trading with minor losses on a day marked by new issues in guilders and Bunds.
One trader said guilder loans endured a bumpy ride with prices bouncing around, lagging Bunds on moves up.
"It's 'buy on the dip' and 'sell on the rally'," he said.
"Everyone is looking at the market, waiting for something to happen," the trader added.
Mortgage bank Achmea Hypo raised 500 million guilders with five and ten-year bonds, while Rabobank issued a 350 million guilder bond due February 2002.
"It's difficult to place them outright. If you want to offer (investors) new paper, they want to sell old paper," he said, adding that this sparked switching out of other Eurobonds.
The German government issued five billion marks of the new 6.0 percent Jan 2007 Bund at a yield of 5.86 percent.
Another trader said trading was busier than recently, noting switching into 2003 Dutch paper from the 2002 maturity for a yield pick-up and switching into 2003 Bunds from guilders.
Dealers said the market was pre-occupied with U.S. data for December this week, particularly figures for employment on Friday and producer prices on Thursday.
